Dependency firewall

Usage: waharoa <COMMAND>

Commands:
  daemon   Run the proxy in the foreground
  doctor   Check whether this machine installs through the proxy
  status   What this build does for each ecosystem, and which streams cover it
  explain  Why a package is allowed or refused
  audit    Work with the audit log
  intel    Read what the intel store records
  policy   Work with policy files
  warm     Ask a running proxy for every artifact a lockfile locks, so each is analysed before a client asks for it. The exit code is the OR of 1 for a failure and 2 for an artifact still being analysed, and 4 on its own for an error
  refresh  Load OSV, GitHub, CISA KEV and Datadog intel into the Postgres at WAHAROA_DATABASE_URL
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

Proxy configuration, all through the environment:

  WAHAROA_LISTEN                    address to listen on (default 127.0.0.1:8080)
  WAHAROA_UPSTREAM_NPM              npm registry to forward to (default https://registry.npmjs.org)
  WAHAROA_UPSTREAM_PYPI             PyPI simple index to forward to (default https://pypi.org/simple)
  WAHAROA_PUBLIC_URL                address written into artifact URLs, and therefore
                                    into lockfiles. Defaults to each request's own Host,
                                    which is rarely what you want.
  WAHAROA_ARTIFACT_ORIGINS          comma-separated origins this proxy also serves
  WAHAROA_ALLOW_DIRECT_ORIGINS      comma-separated origins the proxy does not serve and
                                    permits anyway, fetched directly and unexamined
  WAHAROA_REWRITE_ARTIFACTS=0       do not point artifact URLs at the proxy. pnpm and
                                    yarn then fetch artifacts without the proxy seeing
                                    them.
  WAHAROA_CA_BUNDLE                 PEM bundle for the upstream connection
  WAHAROA_CA_BUNDLE_EXCLUSIVE=1     trust only that bundle, not the public roots
  WAHAROA_MAX_METADATA_BYTES        ceiling on a metadata document (default 64 MiB)
  WAHAROA_MAX_RECORDS               package records held in memory (default 50000)
  WAHAROA_MAX_VERIFIED              verified artifact digests remembered (default 50000)
  WAHAROA_DATABASE_URL              Postgres holding intel from `waharoa refresh`. With a
                                    policy, known_malware is enforced from it, and a
                                    store that cannot answer is a 503
  WAHAROA_GITHUB_TOKEN              token `waharoa refresh` reads GitHub's Advisory
                                    Database with. Unset, that one stream does not load
                                    and the others still do
  WAHAROA_SNAPSHOT_DIR              directory `waharoa refresh` keeps each snapshot in,
                                    for `policy diff --snapshot`. Unset, none is kept
  WAHAROA_SNAPSHOT_LIMIT            most snapshots kept there; a refresh removes older ones (default 30)
  WAHAROA_POLICY                    path to a policy file. Loaded, validated and
                                    enforced. Startup reports which checks can fire
  WAHAROA_AUDIT_LOG                 path for one JSON line per policy decision,
                                    appended. Refuses to start if it cannot be opened
  WAHAROA_EXPIRY_CEILING_DAYS       how many days ahead a `packages` entry may be dated (default 90)
  WAHAROA_MAX_CONCURRENT_METADATA   metadata documents decoded at once (default 8)
  WAHAROA_SPOOL_DIR                 directory an artifact is written to while it is
                                    analysed. Locked; spool files left in it are removed
                                    at startup (default waharoa-spool in the OS temp dir)
  WAHAROA_MAX_ARTIFACT_BYTES        ceiling on an artifact written to the spool (default 1024 MiB)
  WAHAROA_MAX_CONCURRENT_ANALYSES   artifacts analysed at once (default 8)
  WAHAROA_MAX_TRAFFIC_CLIENTS       client names counted apart in a traffic window (default 256)
  WAHAROA_REFUSAL_STATUS            status a refusal answers with, per client, e.g.
                                    "default=403,npm/pnpm=451" (default 403)
  WAHAROA_REFUSE_UNSERVABLE=0       forward versions whose artifacts this proxy cannot
                                    see, instead of removing them from the metadata
  WAHAROA_MODE                      "observe" serves what the policy refuses and logs it (default enforce)
  HTTPS_PROXY                       forward proxy for upstream https; the lowercase name
                                    is read too
  HTTP_PROXY                        forward proxy for upstream http; the lowercase name
                                    is read too
  NO_PROXY                          hosts fetched without the forward proxy, comma-separated;
                                    the lowercase name is read too
  WAHAROA_LOG_FORMAT                "json" writes one OpenTelemetry log record per line (default text)
  RUST_LOG                          log filter, in tracing's syntax (default waharoa=info)
  WAHAROA_DEFER_TEST                DEBUG BUILDS ONLY: answer every matching request with
                                    a deferral instead of fetching, so client retry
                                    behaviour can be measured. `<status>:<seconds|none>:
                                    <metadata|artifact|all>[:<seconds>]`, e.g.
                                    "429:1:artifact" or "503:1:all:8"
